candidate_facts.text: The Korean War led to a significant increase in military spending.
The Korean War contributed to the development of a powerful military-industrial complex.
The dismissal of General Douglas MacArthur by President Truman triggered a political firestorm.
The dismissal of General Douglas MacArthur significantly damaged Truman's approval ratings.
The dismissal of General Douglas MacArthur contributed to the end of Truman's presidency.
The firing of General Douglas MacArthur by President Truman for insubordination was highly unpopular.
The firing of General Douglas MacArthur shocked the American political system.
The Korean War intensified public fear of communist subversion.
The Korean War led to investigations by the House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC).
The Korean War led to a belief in widespread communist infiltration within American institutions.

sub_narrative: "What impact did the Korean War have on US politics?"
